title: Literal Equations: Solving Formulas for a Variable
seo_title: Algebra I Literal Equations Worksheets (TEKS A.12E)
standard_text: A.12E solve mathematic and scientific formulas, and other literal equations, for a specified variable
meta_desc: Free Algebra I literal equation worksheets for Texas TEKS A.12E: solve formulas for a variable, standard form to slope-intercept form, science formulas and applications. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Treat the other letters like numbers.
key_sub: A = lw, so w = A ÷ l.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Treat the other letters like numbers.
  • Undo operations in reverse order: first addition or subtraction, then multiplication or division.
  • Do the same thing to both sides and to every term.
  • If the variable appears twice, collect those terms and factor it out.

Examples

Example

Solve A = lw for w

divide both sides by l

Answer: w = A ÷ l

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Undoing in the wrong orderUndo + and − first.
Dividing only one termDivide every term.
Losing a negative signCheck by putting values in.

items.e: Squaring is undone by taking the square root.
Divide by 3, then add 2: t = w/3 + 2.

items.q: To solve y = 4x + 7 for x, what should you do first?
items.e: Undo the operations in reverse order: the + 7 was last, so subtract 7 first.

items.q: Marcus solves y = 2x + 6 for x and gets x = y/2 − 6. What is the correct answer?
items.e: Subtract 6 first, then divide everything by 2: x = (y − 6) ÷ 2. Marcus only divided y.
Add x and subtract y: x = 5 − y.
